decisions.decision: G1 for M5 is judged ONLY against the six properties P1..P6 of docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 12.8. The judge writes one check per property, named p1..p6, and no check anywhere in the record makes the completeness of a task list a condition of the verdict. The section 2 task table, the count of M5 remediation tasks, and the status of any individual task are recorded as provenance in a separate check and are explicitly declared non-conditions. The judge may not add a seventh property.
decisions.rationale: Section 12.1 measured that the old G1 ('every task of the milestone is complete') is the node of the positive feedback loop: each newly discovered task automatically tightened the gate, so discovery converted into unreachability (08-24 to 08-26: +48 complete, +48 new, fan-out 1.0, 40 planned tasks became 96). G1 v2 replaces the task set with a property set precisely so that a task that binds to no property cannot stop the gate. Adding a property at judging time would re-create the ratchet inside the judgment that was written to stop it.

decisions.decision: For each of P1..P6 the judge states, in the check's own summary, (i) satisfied or not satisfied, (ii) SAFETY CLAIM or LIVENESS REQUIREMENT, and (iii) the ground. For a safety claim the ground is an assertion that proves the guard REFUSES, cited as file and line, re-executed at the judging commit, and it must be an enumeration or a closure -- never a single occurrence. For a liveness requirement the ground is that the thing HAPPENED, carried by an eligible evidence record. Section 12.8 assigns the kinds: P1 and P2 are safety, P3 P4 P5 P6 are liveness. The judge re-derives the kind from the wording of the property rather than copying the table, and reports any disagreement.
decisions.rationale: Section 8.1 was written because the first M5 gate read a safety claim ('only a candidate with full capability evidence becomes Stable') as a liveness requirement and failed the milestone for an event that the condition never required. Its two errata sharpen this in both directions: erratum 1 says the section adjudicated completion condition 4 only, so condition 1 (dogfood) stays liveness and is failed for want of an eligible ground rather than for a low success count; erratum 2 says the section's own first ground violated its own reverse constraint, because A17's positive half was one promotion in a composed tree and its negative half one refusal set -- a single occurrence proves nothing about the exhaustiveness of a refusal. The replacement grounds were closure enumerations. A judge that does not state the kind per property will make one of those two mistakes again.

decisions.decision: P1 ('a docs-only drift stops promotion', safety) is judged at internal/release/pipeline.go:39, where Pipeline.Promote calls VerifySource BEFORE PromotionGate (line 52), Store.Put (55) and Router.Promote (58) -- measured at cd48424, so the refusal precedes the gate, the store and the route, and a refusal cannot leave a half-promoted route. The two assertions section 12.8 names verify at the exact lines it gives: internal/release/pipeline_test.go:60 is TestPipelinePromoteRefusesFabricatedMatchingDocsDigest (a fabricated MATCHING DocsDigest is still refused) and :101 is TestPipelinePromoteDocsDriftHermeticWithNegativeControl (hermetic, with a mandatory negative control). The judge re-reads all four numbers at its own judging commit and reports any movement, and runs the two tests by name.
decisions.rationale: Every line number in a packet is stale by construction. I measured these four (39, 52/55/58, 60, 101) with sed and grep at cd48424 and they agree with section 12.8, but V2-089 is running concurrently and the coordinator will merge V2-090, V2-091 and V2-095 before the judging commit. A binding that section 12.8 asserts and the judge merely copies is not a measurement; the instruction to check the binding rather than trust it is what makes the safety verdict the judge's own.

decisions.decision: P2 ('a candidate without full capability evidence does not become Stable', safety) is judged at internal/domain/release.go:100 -- the loop at 98-102 returns the wrapped ErrEvidenceIncomplete naming the missing capability by name -- with the three assertions section 12.8 names: internal/domain/release_test.go:122 (TestPromotionRejectionsIsolateEachRefusalClass; I measured exactly 12 rows and 12 DISTINCT rejection kinds in the block 122-225, which is section 8.1's '12 refusal classes'), :230 (the capability closure, a 16384-cell grid) and :372 (the identity closure over 8 statuses times the identity field mask). The judge counts the rows and the kinds itself. It is FORBIDDEN to carry P2 on the dogfood exercise's promotability-positive or promotability-negative subtests (measured at internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:378 and :379), or on the V2-022 A17 check, or on any single promotion or single refusal.
decisions.rationale: This is section 8.1 erratum 2 applied at the exact place it was violated. The reason it can be applied without weakening anything is measured: the closure enumerations are inside internal/domain, so make check re-executes them at the judging commit under G6a, whereas A17 sits inside a live record whose result is partial and whose freshness is gone. The stronger ground is also the cheaper one.

decisions.decision: P3 ('a transition the domain models has a path to it other than a test', liveness, and section 12.1 requires it in every property set) is judged by a table the judge builds itself: for each of the nine RequirementCommandKind values declared at internal/domain/model.go:437-445 -- start-framing, ready, start, wait, needs-input, recover, evaluate, pause, cancel -- the count of non-test lines that ISSUE that command (a 'Kind:' composite literal), not merely mention it. Measured at cd48424: StartFraming 1 issuer (internal/application/framing.go:191), ReadyCommand 2 (human_input.go:648, framing.go:374), Start 1 (service.go:1390), NeedInput 1 (human_input.go:519), and Wait, Recover, Evaluate, Pause, Cancel ZERO -- four of nine reachable, five of nine unreachable. The judge additionally measures the promotion path: at cd48424 release.NewPipeline and Pipeline.Promote have ZERO non-test callers, and application.AttachReleaseObserver has zero non-test callers. P3 is satisfied only if every one of the nine has at least one non-test issuer and the promotion path has at least one non-test caller; otherwise P3 fails and the judge names the empty rows.
decisions.rationale: Section 12.8 binds P3 to V2-084, V2-089, V2-090 and V2-091, and section 12.1 records that all three of the tasks it merged were saying the same sentence ('no code outside a test constructs it', 'nothing can reach because the pass has no caller', 'the only thing that drives one today is a test'). That sentence is a grep, so P3 must be judged as a grep and not as 'those four tasks are complete' -- which would be judging against a task list, the one thing G1 v2 forbids. Measured status at cd48424: V2-084 complete, V2-089 running, V2-090 blocked, V2-091 blocked, so five empty rows is the expected reading today and the table is the instrument that decides whether the merges actually closed them. METHODOLOGY, measured: an unanchored grep for 'domain.RequirementStart' returns 4 lines because it also matches RequirementStartFraming, and 'domain.RequirementCancel' returns 1 line which is internal/application/readmodels.go:310 comparing the STATUS RequirementCancelled. Word-boundary anchoring gives 2 and 0. Both of V2-095's A2(a) expectations are therefore right only under anchoring, and a judge using the unanchored form would read a phantom issuer.

decisions.decision: P4 (owner can read a Backlog longer than one page), P5 (owner can ask and be answered) and P6 (repository registration and the owner documents agree with the behaviour) are liveness. Each is judged by TWO things that must both hold: (i) the capability-named check inside the M5live record carries status passed -- cap-backlog-visibility for P4, cap-human-input-request for P5, cap-repository-registration AND cap-user-documentation for P6; and (ii) the non-test site that makes the state reachable, cited by file and line. The judge measures (ii) itself: the paging cursor repair is at internal/store/firestore/store.go:638-640 (documentIDCursor, whose comment block at 630-637 records the defect it closes), and the needs-input issuer is at internal/application/human_input.go:519 with its framing issuer at internal/application/framing.go:191. If the record's check is passed but no non-test site exists, P4/P5/P6 are NOT satisfied and the judge says which half failed.
decisions.rationale: Both halves are needed for a different reason. Without (i) the property has no live ground and G3 item 3 forbids substituting a unit test. Without (ii) a passing live check could be carried by a test-only path, which is exactly the defect P3 exists to name -- so a property judged only from the record could pass while the transition it claims stays unreachable. DISAGREEMENT, measured: V2-095's work order locates the cursor repair at 'store.go:637'; at cd48424 line 637 is the last line of the comment and the function is at 638. The claim survives, the number moves by one.

decisions.decision: G2 is judged by measurement over .agents/v2/evidence/index.json: every entry's evidence_hash equals the sha256 of the file it names, the set of *.json files directly under .agents/v2/evidence/ equals the set of paths the index names, and -- the decisive part -- the entry or entries whose component is exactly release-live-dogfood must include at least one whose result is passed. Measured at cd48424: 171 entries, 0 hash mismatches, bijection true, index is 1 line, and component release-live-dogfood has EXACTLY ONE entry, ev-v2-022-release-live-dogfood, result partial; component provider-live-claude-dogfood likewise exactly one, ev-v2-022-provider-live-claude-dogfood, result partial. No passed record for either component exists among the 171. A provider-live-claude record (ev-v2-063, ev-v2-075, ev-v2-080 are the three passed ones) may NOT stand in.
decisions.rationale: This is where M5 died twice and section 8.2 is the postmortem: section 5 makes release-live-dogfood the mandatory live component of M5, and a record whose component is a different name is a different record no matter how fresh it is. V2-081 recorded that its own work order asserted G6b was closed by V2-080 and that this was false because V2-080 re-observed ./internal/runner's TestProviderLiveVerticalSlice under component provider-live-claude. The judge must therefore look up the component name in section 5's table FIRST, then look up the entry by that name, and treat any other record as inadmissible for this gate.

decisions.decision: The judge does not read V2-095's claim about the split. It re-derives the partition from contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json with TWO independent predicates and requires them to agree. Predicate A, over external_dependencies: 'Google Cloud Run' in systems, or both 'codex' and 'opencode' in providers. Predicate B, over the promotion_prerequisites strings: the text names Cloud Run, or names codex and opencode. Measured at cd48424, both predicates give the identical partition -- 4 deferred to D1 (cap-preview-operation, cap-stable-promotion, cap-loop-control, cap-loop-self-update), 3 deferred to M6 (cap-autonomous-resolution, cap-shared-resource-allocation, cap-provider-operation), 5 eligible (cap-repository-registration, cap-requirement-intake, cap-backlog-visibility, cap-human-input-request, cap-user-documentation), 12 total. The REVERSE CONSTRAINT is measured in the same pass and both ways: not one of the 5 eligible names Cloud Run, codex or opencode anywhere in external_dependencies OR in promotion_prerequisites. If the record's 7 skipped checks are not exactly the derived set of 7, or if any of the 5 eligible carries a skipped check, G2 fails.
decisions.rationale: Section 8.3 makes deferral 'a measurable fact derived from the capability's declaration, not a judgement', and its reverse constraint -- the body of the rule -- forbids recording a product gap as a deferral. The only way a judge can honour that is to derive the set from the declaration file rather than accept a producer's list; otherwise the record's own classification becomes its own proof. Two predicates instead of one because a single one can be satisfied by editing one field: contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json is prohibited to V2-095, so both derivations are over ground the producing task could not move, and their agreement is a cross-check that costs one command.

decisions.decision: For the three capabilities deferred to M6 the judge must quote promotion_prerequisites condition 3, not only the providers array. Measured at cd48424, all three declare providers ['codex','claude','opencode'] -- and claude IS authenticated on this machine, so the array alone leaves open the argument 'exercise it with claude and it stops being deferred'. Condition 3 closes that argument by declaration: each of the three says '対象Provider（codex、claude、opencode）の実物へ接続して成功すること', so the capability's own declared prerequisite requires connecting to codex and opencode for real. The judge quotes that clause per capability and separately re-measures, at judging time, that codex and opencode are unauthenticated on this machine -- and records the authentication measurement as CORROBORATION only, never as the derivation.
decisions.rationale: This is the strongest form of the reverse constraint. Section 8.3 says deferral must be derived from the declaration and never from the observation 'we could not reach it'. If the judge derived the M6 three from the machine's authentication state it would be doing exactly what the rule forbids, and the derivation would flip the moment somebody ran codex login. Deriving it from condition 3 makes the deferral a property of the declared contract; the machine state then only confirms that the declared prerequisite is in fact unmet here. This refinement is mine: V2-095's A4 reads external_dependencies.providers only, which is sufficient for the partition but leaves the claude loophole unaddressed.

decisions.decision: G6b is measured on M5's exercise only: TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood in package ./internal/api (internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:286, gates AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_DOGFOOD=1 and AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_PROVIDER=1 plus FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, 17 subtests at lines 364-380 of which 12 are the capability ids), component release-live-dogfood. ./internal/runner's TestProviderLiveVerticalSlice under component provider-live-claude is M3's and is out of scope; the judge states that explicitly and does not measure it as freshness for this gate. The judge recomputes the compiled set mechanically (go list -deps -test over ./internal/api, GoFiles plus CgoFiles plus EmbedFiles of this module only, intersected with git ls-files), compares it path-by-path with the set the record publishes, and only then measures the intersection with the observation-to-judgement diff. Measured at cd48424: the compiled set is 88 paths (internal/runner 20, internal/application 15, internal/api 10, internal/update 8, internal/provider 7, internal/domain 6, internal/release 5, internal/contracts 5, internal/web 4, internal/store/firestore 3, internal/scheduler 3, internal/store/memory 1, internal/quota 1), and the intersection of that set with the diff from ev-v2-022's observation commit 39d2e809b02527d1e8b56f44cbb4fc20473344ef to cd48424 is 34 paths over a 168-path diff.
decisions.rationale: Section 8.2 is Sol's own recorded mistake and it cost a gate: 'before claiming live freshness, look up the mandatory component name for THAT gate in the section 5 table, look up the index entry with that name, and measure with the file set the record's own exercise declares.' The number also shows the old record can never recover: V2-026 measured 26, V2-081 measured 30, I measure 34 -- it grows monotonically because nearly all of internal/application and internal/api is inside the closure. Only a new observation can make G6b passable, which is what V2-095 is for. The set is a PACKAGE closure, so it is identical for M2's TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive, which lives in the same package (both are the only two skipped tests of ./internal/api, measured 2 with both grep patterns); what distinguishes the two exercises is the gate variables and the read-at-run-time group, and the judge should say so rather than pretend the compiled group identifies the exercise.

decisions.decision: The judge measures commit ORDER as part of G6b, not as an afterthought: it reads the observation commit from the record, lists `git diff --name-only <observation> <judging>` in full, transcribes it, and states for every intersecting path whether it landed before or after the observation. Measured at cd48424: 7 of V2-095's 22 allowed_paths are already inside the 88-path set (internal/api/api.go, internal/api/api_test.go, internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go, internal/application/readmodels.go, internal/application/allocation.go, internal/web/owner.html, internal/web/owner.js), and its two NEW files internal/api/ownerdocs.go and ownerdocs_test.go ENTER the set as soon as they exist because they join package internal/api -- so the post-V2-095 compiled set is expected to be about 90, not 88, and the judge must recompute rather than compare against 88. If any path of the intersection landed after the observation, G6b fails regardless of the nature of the change, and the judge does not get to argue that a change was harmless.
decisions.rationale: Section 9.3 and the G6b revision both say the same thing: what decides the order of a live observation is not preference but the measured intersection with the exercise file set, and 'the live task completion convention forbids editing a file the exercise compiles after measuring its key in the same task'. V2-063 obeyed it and the coordinator broke it at integration with one doc comment, which failed M3's gate. DISAGREEMENT, measured: I was told V2-095's edits intersect the set in 11 paths including the exercise's own test file. At cd48424 the intersection of its declared allowed_paths with the compiled set is 7, becoming 9 once the two new internal/api files exist; 11 is reachable only by also counting read-at-run-time members (contracts/release-contract/foundation.json and the two docs/preview files), which live in a different group of the artifact and are governed by V2-095's A20 bound instead. Both numbers are reported and the judge measures its own.

decisions.decision: An empty intersection is admissible only alongside a positive control the judge runs itself: a fictional diff list, editing no tracked file, naming internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go, one internal/application source inside the set, and one internal/web embedded asset, which must print all three with a non-zero count -- and a negative control over real diff lines outside the set which must print zero. The judge records all three numbers and the argv of each. It also recomputes the published set and reports the path-level difference, if any, against its own derivation.
decisions.rationale: The G6b revision states in terms that the rule permits measurement and not argument, and that live evidence which skips the measurement does not satisfy G6b. A zero from a broken pipeline is indistinguishable from a zero from a clean tree: comm over an empty file, a mis-sorted file, or a path-prefix mismatch all print zero. V2-081 ran controls for the record it examined (positive 4, negative 0) and that is why its 'fresh' verdict about V2-080 is believable even though its verdict about M5 was a failure.

decisions.decision: The judge verifies BOTH records V2-095 issues and states in the record, in plain words, that one of them is not guarded by any machine check and why that is accepted. Measured at cd48424: internal/contracts/provider_preflight.go:160 is the only HasPrefix(component, ...) site and its literal is 'provider-live-'; the entries it selects have their provider-preflight artifact binding and their approved_at-before-observed_at ordering enforced by CheckProviderPreflightLedger. ev-v2-095-provider-live-claude-dogfood (component provider-live-claude-dogfood) IS selected. ev-v2-095-release-live-dogfood (component release-live-dogfood) is NOT. Widening the prefix is PROHIBITED: ev-v2-022-release-live-dogfood carries exactly 4 artifact_refs (real-tree-candidate-bundle-digest, real-tree-candidate-contract-digest, real-tree-candidate-docs-digest, release-contract-foundation-json) and none of them is a provider-preflight ref, so widening would immediately fail an existing record and turn internal/contracts red. The judge verifies the release-live record's own self-imposed binding by recomputing the sha256 of the preflight record's bytes and comparing it, and records that this comparison is done by the record and by the judge, by nobody else.
decisions.rationale: Section 9.6.1 is the measurement and section 12.4 is the prohibition: making a rule wider and thereby invalidating an existing observation is retroactive application, and the invalidation would be caused by the rule change rather than by anything observed. DISAGREEMENT, measured: section 9.6.1 and V2-095's A2(c) both say `grep -rn 'release-live' --include='*.go' .` returns 0 lines. At cd48424 it returns TWO -- internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:2115 and :2180, both string literals naming the evidence id ev-v2-022-release-live-dogfood inside the dogfood test's own synthetic capability fixture. The substantive claim is untouched (no Go code SELECTS on that prefix); the command that returns 0 is the same grep piped through `grep -v _test.go`, and the judge should use the anchored form `grep -n 'HasPrefix(component' internal/contracts/provider_preflight.go` for the claim it actually needs.

decisions.decision: G6a is satisfied by a green `make check` at the judging commit on a clean tracked tree, run by the judge itself. Because make check emits no 'FAILS 0' line, the verdict is the conjunction of three measured signals: zero lines matching ^FAIL, gitleaks printing 'no leaks found', and 'workflow-pins: ... no disagreement' (the last of check's prerequisites, so its presence proves the target ran to completion). Per-component evidence key equality is PROVENANCE, not a verdict: the judge does not re-derive the 23 component keys as a freshness claim and does not treat key movement as a finding. It may transcribe one key as corroboration. Measured at cd48424: `make evidence-keys` reports 23 selected components and api = 730944a79feeccaa04d32aa24c574644ab6ac2c9b0f4e88aebc2a51aed637b01.
decisions.rationale: The G6a/G6b split exists because V2-045 widened evidenceKey to the transitive closure of dependency roots, after which almost any commit moves almost every key -- M3's gate failed on exactly that, from one doc comment. For checks that make check re-executes, the claim is re-proved every commit, so the recorded key is the record of provenance and not the gate. Re-deriving all 23 keys and reporting movement would manufacture a finding out of the very phenomenon the rule was rewritten to neutralise, and would tempt the judge to demand a re-issue that section 12.4 forbids.

decisions.decision: The judge separates the GO TEST layer (lines matching a SKIP pattern in a go test -v transcript) from the RECORD layer (a check whose status field is 'skipped'), states the separation explicitly, and records both. Every count is recorded WITH the pattern that produced it, because two different patterns are both correct: measured at cd48424 for ./internal/store/firestore with no emulator, `grep -c '^--- SKIP'` gives 26 (top level) and `grep -cE '^ *--- SKIP'` gives 49 (with subtests), alongside 10 PASS and a vacuous 'ok ... 0.015s'; for ./internal/api with the live gates unset both patterns give 2, and those two are TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood and TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive. At the record layer, the seven skipped capability checks of the M5live record are a classification of SUBTESTS THAT RAN -- the exercise has 17 subtests including one per capability id -- and the judge must verify that the live transcript's SKIP count for the exercise is zero while seven record checks are skipped, and must state that no skipped check is counted as a pass.
decisions.rationale: G7's whole content is that a skip is never a pass, and its failure mode here is structural rather than careless: section 8.3 makes 'skipped' the representation of ineligible-by-declaration at the record layer, and the check status enum has no other member, so the same word means two different things one layer apart. The vacuous 'ok 0.015s' next to 49 skips is the exact shape G7 exists to refuse, and it is inside make check's own `go test ./...`, which is why the emulator-gated component target has to be part of the green verdict the judge relies on.

decisions.decision: The judge measures supersession itself rather than asserting it. The machine definition is at internal/contracts/contracts_test.go:279-296 (supersededTaskIDs: a task id referenced from the repair_of or input_refs of any COMPLETE task) and it is enforced at assertSupersededDependencies only for queued or running dependents. Measured at cd48424: 94 task-state files, 72 complete, 15 blocked, 1 running, 6 FAILED (V2-007, V2-018, V2-023, V2-024, V2-026, V2-081); nothing depends on V2-026 or V2-081, so no machine check fires for this chain either way. Literally, V2-026 is referenced only from V2-028 (blocked) input_refs and V2-081 (failed) repair_of, and V2-081 only from V2-092 (blocked) repair_of and V2-095 (blocked) input_refs. So: V2-095 completing supersedes V2-081 literally; V2-092 completing supersedes V2-081 literally; V2-026 becomes superseded only under the TRANSITIVE reading (V2-092 complete -> V2-081 -> its repair_of names V2-026), which is precisely the reading section 6 itself uses to settle V2-023 through V2-025 -> V2-024 -> V2-023. The judge states which reading it applies, applies it consistently, and records that no machine check enforces it.
decisions.rationale: G4 keeps a gate blocked while an unsettled failed task remains, and V2-092 is the third M5 gate: V2-026 failed on four substantive grounds, V2-081 failed on two. Claiming 'the chain is resolved' without measuring would be exactly the kind of inherited assertion V2-081 caught in its own work order. Measured disagreement: I was told V2-026 failed on four checks; the record has 13 checks of which FIVE carry status failed -- g2, g6a, g6b, m5-completion-condition-mapping and gate-verdict. Four is the count of substantive grounds and the fifth is the verdict itself; V2-081's own prose says four. Also section 6's 'the existing three failed tasks' is now six.

decisions.decision: The record states, as its own check, that under section 12.10 M5's remediation budget stands at 5 of 5 (V2-084, V2-089, V2-090, V2-091, V2-095) and that a sixth remediation task is NOT an available outcome. The judge proposes no task id anywhere in the record, in any form -- not as a suggestion, not as 'a follow-up would be needed', not as a reserved number. If the gate fails for want of work, the record says so in exactly those terms and adds the sentence that section 12.7 requires: this is a signal that the milestone is mis-cut, and the decision about the cut belongs to the coordinator, not to this gate.
decisions.rationale: Section 12.7 fixed the ceiling at five BEFORE it was applied, and section 12.10 measured that M5 landed exactly on the boundary after the V2-091/092/093 merge -- and that the unmerged shape would have tripped it. That is the evidence the rule was not written to fit. V2-081's own record ends with a REMEDIATION paragraph describing the task M5 needed; that paragraph is why V2-095 exists and it consumed the last unit of budget. A judge that writes another one converts its own failure into the +1 that section 12.0 measured as the mechanism keeping the remaining count flat at fan-out 1.0.

decisions.decision: The acceptance criteria specify the FAIL as completely as the pass. On any unsatisfied condition the judge still delivers exactly one record: result 'failed', every check present (no check omitted because the verdict is already decided), the failing check(s) named as THE ground with the measurement that establishes it, a gate-verdict check with status failed that enumerates the satisfied and the unsatisfied conditions separately, an explicit statement that no Stable promotion is decided and that release_eligible stays false, and an explicit statement that a failed V2-092 leaves V2-081 unresolved and requires the coordinator to name a successor -- while proposing no task id. On a pass the same record carries result 'passed', and the complete transition's reason (written by the coordinator, not the judge) must contain the literal string 'gate M5 passed' and the list of evidence ids the verdict rests on.
decisions.rationale: A packet whose acceptance criteria only describe success turns the judge into an advocate: the cheapest way to satisfy it becomes finding a reading in which everything holds. M5 has failed twice and each failure produced a usable record precisely because the record itself was the deliverable. Section 4 also makes the reason string the canonical record of a gate pass, with no dedicated field, so the pass path has a second artifact the judge does not own -- which is another reason the failure path must be fully written down in the part the judge does own.

decisions.decision: allowed_paths contains exactly two entries: .agents/v2/evidence/V2-092-m5-gate.json and .agents/v2/evidence/index.json. Every source and test directory is named in prohibited_paths explicitly, together with contracts/**, ci/**, Makefile, docs/**, scripts/**, .github/**, every other task's packet and evidence, and .agents/v2/task-state/**. A path this packet's prose mentions but allowed_paths omits is PROHIBITED -- the whitelist wins over the prose. The index append is a single-line compact JSON write of exactly one new entry with release_eligible false, no other task's entry touched, no reordering.
decisions.rationale: The judge's own findings are all repairs it must not perform: the check that does not reach release-live- records, the empty P3 rows, the false DECLARATION-GAP row, the roadmap condition bound to no property. Every one of them is a one-line edit away, and a judge that fixes what it measures is no longer measuring. Making the boundary a build-level fact rather than a request is also what keeps this gate from touching task-state, which is the coordinator's, and from touching the record the concurrent V2-089 implementer is producing. The index schema pins release_eligible to the constant false, so 'landing the milestone' cannot and must not mean flipping it.

decisions.decision: The judge records the mapping from roadmap M5's four completion conditions to P1..P6 as provenance: condition 3 ('a docs-only drift stops promotion') is P1, condition 4 ('only a candidate with full capability evidence becomes Stable') is P2, condition 1 ('dogfood this Foundation Repository as the Preview target') is liveness carried by the M5live record, and condition 2 ('break Preview deliberately and resume a Requirement on the old Stable') is bound to NO property in section 12.8. The judge names condition 2's actual ground -- the dogfood exercise's channel-break-and-resume subtest, measured at internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go:376 -- reports whether that subtest passed, and states plainly that its outcome does NOT change the G1 verdict, because G1 v2 defines the gate by the declared property set. It does not add a P7 and it does not propose a task.
decisions.rationale: Refusing to notice the gap would be dishonest and inventing a property to cover it would be the ratchet. Section 12.4 settles which one applies: rules apply at their version and are not applied retroactively, and section 12.8's property set is the M5 rule of record. So the honest handling is to record the unbound condition, name where its evidence lives, and leave the decision about whether the property set is complete with the coordinator -- which is also the shape section 12.7 prescribes for 'the milestone may be mis-cut'.

risks: The judge inherits a number instead of measuring it. Every number in this packet was measured at cd48424 and every one of them can move: V2-089 is running in another worktree and V2-090, V2-091 and V2-095 land before the judging commit. V2-086 reported nineteen disagreements against its own packet, V2-084 fourteen, V2-085 twelve, and V2-095's designer caught four of Sol's plus a false row in the gap ledger. Mitigation: A2 requires re-measurement of every listed value with the command recorded, and a report of BOTH values for every disagreement.

The judge measures the wrong exercise. This is the mistake that failed V2-081: ./internal/runner's TestProviderLiveVerticalSlice belongs to M3 and re-observing it moves nothing for M5. Mitigation: A11 makes the section 5 lookup the first step and requires the record's component name to be quoted before any measurement.

The 5/7/0 split is accepted from V2-095's own record. Then the record classifies itself and section 8.3's reverse constraint is unenforced. Mitigation: A9 derives the partition twice from a declaration file that V2-095 is prohibited from editing, and fails G2 if the record's skipped set differs by one id.

A product gap arrives dressed as a deferral. The four capabilities section 8.3 measured as M5's own (cap-repository-registration, cap-backlog-visibility, cap-human-input-request, cap-user-documentation) are exactly the ones V2-095 must turn from failed into passed, and the cheapest way to appear to do that is to skip them. Mitigation: those four are in the derived ELIGIBLE set, so a skipped check on any of them is a G2 failure by measurement, not by argument.

G6b passes vacuously. A zero from a mis-sorted or mis-prefixed file set is indistinguishable from a clean one. Mitigation: A11 requires the judge's own recomputation, a path-level comparison with the published set, a positive control that must print three paths, and a negative control that must print zero.

The commit order was broken at integration. The M3 gate failed exactly this way, from one doc comment landing after the observation. Measured: 7 of V2-095's allowed_paths are already inside the 88-path set and its two new internal/api files enter it on creation. Mitigation: A11 requires the full observation-to-judgement diff transcribed and each intersecting path attributed to before or after the observation.

The judge repairs what it measures. The reach of provider_preflight.go:160, the empty P3 rows, the false DECLARATION-GAP row about domain.PriorityAssessment, and roadmap condition 2's missing binding are all one edit away. Mitigation: allowed_paths has two entries, every source and test tree is prohibited by name, and A18 requires findings to be recorded as facts with no task id.

The judge proposes a sixth remediation task. Section 12.10 puts M5 at 5 of 5, so that proposal is the +1 that section 12.0 measured as the mechanism holding the remaining count flat. Mitigation: an explicit prohibition, a required sentence about the milestone being mis-cut instead, and no task-id-shaped string anywhere in the record.

A skipped check is read as a pass. 'skipped' means ineligible-by-declaration at the record layer and 'not run' at the go test layer, one layer apart. Mitigation: A16 requires both layers reported with their patterns and their numbers, and a sentence in the record separating them.

make check is red at the judging commit for a reason that has nothing to do with M5 -- V2-026 failed this way, on internal/api importing internal/provider without manifest coverage. G6a is unconditional, so the gate fails. Mitigation: none is available to the judge and none is wanted; the record names the failing package and the failing target and the gate fails on G6a, with the repair belonging to the coordinator.

Section 12.8's own bindings have moved. I verified all four line numbers (pipeline_test.go:60 and :101, release_test.go:122 and :230 and :372, release.go:98-102) at cd48424 and they hold, but the doc is not re-generated. Mitigation: A4 and A5 require the judge to re-locate each assertion by NAME and report the line it actually occupies.

The verdict is written before the checks. A gate that has decided cannot measure. Mitigation: the gate-verdict check is the last acceptance item, it must enumerate satisfied and unsatisfied conditions separately, and A18 specifies the failure deliverable in as much detail as the pass so neither outcome is the cheaper one to write.
